- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model underestimates; adjust up by 1–3% to reflect market resilience.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike followed by a forecast dip, it often overshoots; cap peak forecast at 2–3% below true peak.  
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast.  
- If true outcome exceeds model by >5% over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: next forecast = previous + 0.7×(true - model) to avoid overcorrection.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.8 → -0.4 → +0.6), model fails to capture momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average for smoothing.
